title: Are passion projects important to show quality made ai games?
author: Maidforblood
selftext:
As a solo dev who is passionate about my only game project "maid for blood" i refuse to ship or showcase unfinished release. I can release playable demos thats fine. But i still want to constantly improve my creation i hope one day become successful. It will take time but i will commit to showing i can prove my game will not be labeled as "ai slop" i probably will create a new youtube channel dedicated to maid for blood game project. I already made discord server about my game. I am pretty sure  most of the creators did the same. If your game interest me. I be happy to support it!

  
What do you think? Are you passionate about your game?

comments.author: atluina
comments.body:
It's only "ai slop" if you don't put any effort in and completely rely on AI to make everything. As long as you put in the work and spend effort into that, it will not be an AI slop game, regardless of what ai haters say. 

Being passionate about your game is always a good thing, just don't give up on the project once your passion is gone.

Good luck

replies.author: Maidforblood
replies.body: Well like many ai game dev creators, it can be disheartening when effort is being shown over the course of 3 months or more, and then some random guy can just say "ai slop" when they didnt even bother trying our our games not just mine.  Its only been 3 months in and i still need alot to work with. I am using chatgpt 6 astra + claude code opus 5.5 and elevenlabs, and FL studio to polish the game more as time goes on.

replies.author: J0rdian
replies.body:
If they are not even trying the game it's because it probably looks like AI slop. Presentation and art direction are important and show the effort and passion you have put into your work as well, if it's low quality people will notice right away and not give the rest of the game the benefit of the doubt, as most AI Slop games are easy to spot and not worth playing.

Maybe yours is worth playing and does have a ton of passion and effort behind it. But you have to make it look like it does as well.

comments.author: RegioMamalon666
comments.body: Well, the nothing burger posts have arrived here, it was bound to happen i guess :/

comments.author: Working-Spray-2933
comments.body: I’m very passionate about my game and I stopped posting and removed images of it online bc ppl were copying it and I wanted to see if there were things I could patent first.

replies.author: Maidforblood
replies.body: Whats your game? Tell me about it, i'd like to try it out

replies.author: Working-Spray-2933
replies.body: I can't let u try it out b/c I gotta see if I can patent some things first and then market it!

replies.author: FervantFlea
replies.body: Nintendo can't even stop the flood of blatant Pokemon infringement that is happening right now. Focus on making something people find worth playing, the odds that you invent an engineering process or truly new mechanic that's never been done before that is worth patenting is nonexistant. As someone that's been in tech for a long time, just trust me that patenting in this space is waste of time and money. And even if you did have a patent, are you really going to chase down AI slop legally? Because that's extremely expensive. It'd be easier to just make the best thing that people buy instead of worrying about the copycats.

replies.author: Working-Spray-2933
replies.body: Why not do both? You can make the best thing, and if it is patentable or copyrightable, then just do it. Reeses trademark the color orange.

comments.author: OhGoodGames
comments.body:
Absolutely. My current project is purely a passion project. I'm building a Hybrid 3D/Glyph renderer and lightweight engine. But I'm limiting myself by building it entirely on a legion go, with the intention to make a powerful, lightweight engine that is built around PC handheld specs and development.

And I've fallen into a very unique art direction that I'm iterating on every day because of the development limitations I've set for myself. I've had a few people reach out and just this morning I was contacted by Youtube Playables regarding publishing (could be a scam, I haven't looked into it yet).

But this unique \*thing\* i've made has caught some attention because it's eye catching and not really being done much in game development. I have re-iterated that I don't even have a game yet, I'm simply building an engine and experimenting. But that in itself has driven interest towards me.

While I do feel that people may be able to mimic my look, I don't know if they could actually reverse engineer it themselves at this point without significant development time or my source code. I don't believe there are any games or open source projects that have a renderer that works the same way as mine, or the additional reforming tech that makes it clear and smooth in motion. But that is also probably my ego speaking and someone will just go ahead and do it with one prompt lol.

https://reddit.com/link/1xgpb02/video/91k22dn9d1yh1/player

replies.author: Maidforblood
replies.body: that looks cool not gonna lie!  looking forward how your project goes my friend!
